note: One case per Rust test of effect/emit.rs (emit_with_object_first_arg_is_a_hard_error_naming_the_missing_event, emit_with_number_first_arg_is_a_hard_error, emit_with_valid_identifier_stays_clean) and the orbital-cli test validate_emit_missing_event_name.rs (the object-first emit is ORB_EFF_EMIT_INVALID_NAME with the message and suggestion it pins), plus the arity, identifier, list, boolean and null forms of validate_emit and the effect-sequencing walk of validate_effect_in (paths .do[i], .then, .else, .then[i], .body[i] and [k] for a branch written as a list of effects). Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion the Rust validator reports. The emit config blocks of the async operators (validate_emit_config) are checked by those operators' own lints. The effects are flattened by std-orb-effect-leaves: the rule asks with EFFECT_LEAVES_EXPAND and checks the leaves it answers. A branch that is null is no leaf, so a null else is neither a finding nor an unchecked node.

findings.suggestion: Write `(emit EVENT_NAME { … })` — the event name comes first, then the payload object. The event must be declared in the trait's `emits` block.
